questions.question: When you reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as another vehicle, what should happen?

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
Flash your headlights to tell the other vehicle to go.
Continue through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection with no signs or traffic lights, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wearing bright, reflective clothing while riding keeps you safe at any time.

questions.question: What helps reduce the chance of a crash?
questions.explanation: To reduce crashes, be visible, signal your moves, keep safe distance, look ahead at least 12 seconds, spot hazards early, and be ready to react to changes.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, where should you position yourself?

options.text: In the part of the lane where other drivers can see you easiest.
In the part of the lane closest to the traffic control device.
On the outside edge of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the part of the lane where other drivers can see you easiest.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection, position yourself so other drivers see you as soon as possible.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass. Speeding up only makes them tailgate you at the higher speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: When should you always do a head check?
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any vehicle. Turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes, merging, or passing. Mirrors alone are not enough.

questions.question: What should you do when riding on a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, reduce your speed, avoid sudden moves, and use both brakes carefully.

questions.question: Do motorcycle mirrors have blind spots?

options.text: No, because motorcycles are smaller than cars.

questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any vehicle. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: What should you check when choosing a helmet?

options.text: It has no cracks or damage.

questions.correctAnswerText: It has no cracks or damage.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards. It should fit snugly and have no cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: What lane position should you choose?

options.text: One that helps you avoid road hazards.
One that hides you from other drivers.
One that puts you directly next to another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: One that helps you avoid road hazards.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that helps you avoid road hazards. Always keep safe space around your motorcycle.

questions.question: A motorcycle must have all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: In Idaho, motorcycles must have fenders on both wheels, a brake on at least one wheel, a headlight, a horn, a mirror, a muffler, a brake light, a taillight, and at least one rear reflector. If you carry passengers, you must also have a passenger seat and footrests.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Only wear a jacket at night.
Only wear a jacket if it is cold outside.

questions.explanation: Always wear a sturdy jacket with long sleeves when riding a motorcycle, even if the weather is warm.

questions.question: Riding right after rain starts can be difficult because:

options.text: Other drivers may not react quickly to the rain.
Other drivers do not drive fast enough in wet weather.

questions.explanation: When rain first starts, the pavement is very slippery. Oil from vehicles has not yet washed away, and it mixes with the water to create a slippery surface.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that a divided roadway is coming.

questions.question: The faster you drink alcohol:

options.text: The faster your body removes it.
The faster it builds up in your body.
The less it affects your body.

questions.correctAnswerText: The faster it builds up in your body.
questions.explanation: The faster you drink, the faster alcohol builds up in your body. Your body removes alcohol at an average rate of one drink per hour. If you drink more than one drink in an hour, alcohol will still be in your system after that hour passes.

questions.question: A rider's boots or shoes should:

options.text: Be made of soft, flexible material.

questions.explanation: Choose sturdy footwear that is high enough to cover and support your ankles. The soles should be hard, durable, and slip-resistant.

questions.question: When riding behind a car in the left third of the lane, the driver can see you in their side mirror. What is a problem with this?

options.text: Most drivers don't check their side mirrors as often as their rearview mirror.
Wind may prevent the use of a side mirror.
Drivers should not use their side mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most drivers don't check their side mirrors as often as their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Most drivers look at their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors. When following a car, ride in the center of the lane. This way, the driver is more likely to see you in the rearview mirror.

questions.question: Head and neck injuries are reduced:
questions.explanation: Head and neck injuries are always a risk when riding a motorcycle, no matter your speed. A properly fitted, quality helmet greatly reduces the risk of head and neck injuries.

questions.question: If vehicles or hazards are to your right, which side of the lane should you ride on?
questions.explanation: Position yourself to have the most space. If hazards are on your left, ride on the right side of your lane. If hazards are on your right, ride on the left side of your lane.

questions.question: Taking a turn too fast can cause a rider to:

options.text: Drift into another lane of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drift into another lane of traffic.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast can cause you to cross into another lane or leave the road. Always slow down before entering a turn or curve.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The traffic light will soon turn red.
The traffic light will soon turn green.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The traffic light will soon turn red.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light warns you that the light is about to turn red. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, continue through.

questions.question: To reduce the chances of a collision, a motorcycle rider should:

options.text: Keep enough space between yourself and other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep enough space between yourself and other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Always keep a safe distance around your motorcycle. Keep this space when following others, being followed, passing, being passed, or sharing lanes.

questions.question: If you have only one drink before riding:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
It can affect your ability to operate a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can affect your ability to operate a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Even one drink can affect your riding skills. If you drink any amount of alcohol, it is not safe to ride.

questions.question: Lanes moving in the same direction are separated by:
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Solid white lines mean you cannot pass. Dashed white lines mean you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: The best footwear for motorcyclists are:
questions.explanation: Leather boots give the best foot protection when riding. Boots should be high and sturdy enough to cover and support your ankles.
